provenance.scope: Single explicit-demand momentum-transfer-rate relation for the owner-supplied ExamSIDE COMEDK machine-gun question.
provenance.deliberately_partial: Collision conservation, centre of mass, rockets and time-varying-force integration are intentionally absent.
provenance.source_authority: The individual ExamSIDE item is owner-approved preparation demand, not Pinnacle school-issued micro-scope.
provenance.review_status: Author-created adaptation; independent academic review remains separate.

gates.title: Average force from momentum transferred per unit time

canonical_concepts.statement: Average force requires momentum change per unit time; one item's momentum alone is not a force.
Identical per-item momentum changes add linearly over a steady counting interval.
Newton-third-law recoil is equal and opposite on the launcher/body, not a cancellation on the emitted item's FBD.

relations.expression: p = m v; F_avg = Delta p / Delta t; steady identical items at rate r: |F_avg| = r |Delta p_item|
relations.meaning: Average external force equals momentum transferred per unit time; steady identical item changes add linearly over the counting interval.
conditions: Momentum and velocity refer to the same chosen item/body and one inertial frame.
The first-slice relation treats the item mass as constant over its stated momentum change.
F_avg is the average net force associated with the stated momentum transfer over Delta t.
For a steady stream of identical items, the per-item momentum change and item rate refer to the same counting interval.
The equal-and-opposite recoil interpretation belongs to the launcher/body on the other side of the interaction, not to the emitted item's own free-body equation.

validity_conditions: Choose the item/body and frame before Delta p.
A time interval or item rate is present before momentum is interpreted as force.
Use the recoil partner on the launcher only after the emitted item's momentum transfer is established.

reasoning_sequence.action: Compute the momentum change of one emitted item in one frame.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: The repeated transfer is built from a definite per-item change.

reasoning_sequence.action: Accumulate identical item changes over the stated time/rate and divide by time.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Average force is momentum change per unit time.

reasoning_sequence.action: Place the equal-and-opposite interaction on the launcher and check force units.
reasoning_sequence.why_valid: Newton III determines the partner body/direction while dimensional analysis checks the rate conversion.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: One bullet's momentum can be equated directly to holding force.
misconceptions.counterexample: Momentum has units kg m/s while force has kg m/s^2.
misconceptions.repair: Introduce the time interval or bullets-per-second rate before interpreting the result as average force.

problem_families.title: Machine-gun / steady ejection average recoil-force questions
hidden_invariants: Force scales linearly with item rate.
Per-item momentum is accumulated before time division.

falsification_cases.mutation: Remove the unit field from the first symbol of the relation.
